rationale: The answer misses the central requested mechanism. Under Irish rules (Reg. 88(1)–(2) of the 2026 regulations and CBI Q&A 1016/1088), 'UCITS ETF' is a required identifier in the name, constitution, prospectus, KID/KIID and marketing materials. The answer instead calls it 'a market term, not a separate UCITS legal category' and treats identification as LEIs, ISINs and tickers, which contradicts the regulatory naming requirement. For a sub-fund with listed and unlisted classes, it says the identifier applies only to the listed class, 'not to the whole sub-fund'. The rules allow it at either sub-fund or listed-class level, provided the classes are clearly distinguished. The answer omits the sub-fund-level option and the requirement to distinguish the classes. It does not address the point that class-level identification already existed in the pre-2026 Q&A, though it also does not wrongly call it new. To its credit, it correctly avoids labelling non-ETF sibling sub-funds or unlisted classes as ETFs, and broadly says only the ETF sub-fund carries the label in a mixed umbrella. These points do not offset the material errors on the core identifier rule.
